info.description: A Django + DRF backend for local events and meetups with PostGIS geospatial search and ingestion/provenance. This schema describes the public, read-only catalog surface a client (e.g. the demo SPA) consumes.

get.description:
Read-only city catalog.

- Search: ``?search=<text>`` matches the city name (prefix/contains).
- Filter: ``?country_code=DE``.
- Order:  ``?ordering=name`` (default) or ``?ordering=-population``.
- Page size: ``?page_size=<n>`` (capped at 1000).
- Full list (no pagination): ``/api/cities/all/`` — returns every active
  city in one response, for clients that want to cache the whole catalog
  (e.g. an offline pick-list / autocomplete).

List, create, retrieve, update and destroy events.

- Filter: ``?category=<id>&category__slug=<slug>&city=<city>&organization=<id>&
  organization_slug=<slug>&event_type=<…>&attendance_mode=<…>&status=<…>&
  starts_at_after=&starts_at_before=``
- Search: ``?search=<text>`` matches title and description.
- Order:  ``?ordering=starts_at`` (or ``-starts_at``).
- Proximity: ``?lat=<lat>&lon=<lon>&radius_km=<km>`` (or ``?near_city=<slug>``)
  returns events within the radius, each annotated with a ``distance`` (km),
  ordered nearest-first. **Online events are excluded** from proximity.
- Lifecycle actions: ``POST /api/events/<id>/publish/``,
  ``/cancel/``, ``/archive/``, ``/revert_to_draft/`` (owner / ``owner_group``
  member / holder of ``events.change_event``).

parameters.name: attendance_mode
parameters.description:
* `physical` - Physical
* `online` - Online
* `hybrid` - Hybrid

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description:
* `meetup` - Meetup
* `conference` - Conference
* `workshop` - Workshop
* `social` - Social
* `other` - Other

get.description:
Submit and read untrusted event observations.

``POST`` submits one observation (forced ``status=pending``); ``bulk/``
submits a list transactionally. List/retrieve let the extractor confirm what
it submitted. Reviewing/promoting is an operator action in the admin.

get.description:
Report ingestion runs.

``POST`` creates a run (defaults to ``running``, ``reported_by`` = caller);
``PATCH`` (or the ``/success/`` / ``/failure/`` actions) finishes it. Finishing
a run also stamps its source's ``last_fetched_at`` / ``next_due_at`` schedule.

prefix.description: Public prefix to identify the key.

City.description: Read-only representation of a city, exposing its centroid as lat/lon.

geoname_id.description: Stable GeoNames id; idempotency key for re-seeding.

DueSource.description:
A source eligible for extraction (approved + active + due).

Read-only; this is the extractor's work queue.

fetch_interval_minutes.description: How often the extractor should revisit this source.

EventObservation.description: Full read of an observation (listing / admin / retrieval).

EventObservationNested.description:
Minimal read-only view of an observation, used on ``Event.promoted_from``.

Deliberately small so the canonical-event payload can't recurse into the
full observation graph.

EventObservationSubmit.description:
The extractor's submit payload for a single observation.

``source`` is required (which source the observation came from); ``run`` is
optional (set when reporting inside a run). ``status`` is forced to
``pending`` — the extractor can never self-promote. ``latitude`` /
``longitude`` are write-only and stored as ``location``.

EventObservationSubmitRequest.description:
The extractor's submit payload for a single observation.

``source`` is required (which source the observation came from); ``run`` is
optional (set when reporting inside a run). ``status`` is forced to
``pending`` — the extractor can never self-promote. ``latitude`` /
``longitude`` are write-only and stored as ``location``.

EventSourceNested.description: Minimal read-only view of an event source, used on ``Event.source``.

IngestionRun.description:
Report an ingestion run.

On create, ``status`` defaults to ``running`` and ``reported_by`` is set by
the view to the calling service account. The extractor later PATCHes the run
to ``succeeded`` / ``failed`` with ``finished_at`` / ``events_found`` /
``error_message``.

``error_message``.
